h1: The 8 Best Printer Stands for Small Spaces of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Compact Printer Stands 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight printer stands and rolling carts for small spaces, from under-desk stands with drawers to slim utility carts and risers.
summary: The HUANUO printer stand is our top pick because it was designed for printers and has cable management, a drawer and locking casters. The YAOHUOO 22 x 15 is the roomier pick for bigger all-in-ones, and the HOOBRO suits dorms. The rolling carts are the flexible storage alternative.
intro: Most people measure the printer and forget to measure the gap it has to live in. A stand that fits the machine but not the space under the desk ends up in the middle of the room, and a printer that needs its paper tray pulled out also needs clearance in front.

We ranked eight options, mixing dedicated printer stands with rolling carts and risers that readers commonly repurpose. Ranking went to how well each fits a printer, how little floor it uses, mobility, storage, and cable control. Several of these were not designed for printers, and we say so where it matters.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: A real printer stand sized for compact and mid-size machines.
products.description:
The HUANUO is a dedicated stand with a 14.1 inch maximum height, a rear cable channel, locking casters and a storage drawer under the top shelf. It fits compact and mid-size printers and costs $25 to $50.

It takes the top spot because it is the one built for a printer, with cord control and a drawer for paper. Next to the rolling carts below, it gives up tiers for a tidier, lower profile that slides under a desk more easily.

Buy it if you want a purpose-built stand. The caveat is that it suits compact to mid-size machines, so very large units may not fit.
products.idealFor: Compact and mid-size printers in a small office.

products.name: YAOHUOO 22x15 Large Printer Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: A bigger top for business-class all-in-ones, on casters.
products.description:
A two-tier rolling stand with a 22 inch by 15 inch tabletop, a built-in drawer and casters. The listing says it fits business-class all-in-one printers. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks below the HUANUO because it lacks the listed cable channel, but it ranks above the HOOBRO since the 22 by 15 top handles wider machines. The tradeoff is more footprint.

Choose it when the printer is the biggest constraint in the room. The caveat is that a larger top uses more floor space than the compact stands.
products.idealFor: Bigger all-in-one printers in small rooms.
products.skipIf: Floor space is the tightest constraint.

products.name: HOOBRO 2-Tier Printer Stand with Charging Station
products.verdict: A compact under-desk shelf with a charging station built in.
products.description:
A two-tier open shelf stand with a built-in charging station shelf and a compact under-desk profile, finished in rustic brown and black. It is suited to compact printers and costs $25 to $50.

It ranks third because the compact size limits which printers fit, and open shelves offer less cover than a drawer. What it adds is a spot to charge devices beside the printer.

It suits studio apartments and dorm-size rooms. The caveat is its focus on compact printers only.
products.idealFor: Dorms and studios with a compact printer.

products.name: Simple Houseware 3-Tier Heavy Duty Metal Utility Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A flexible metal cart that holds a printer plus supplies.
products.description:
A three-tier heavy-duty metal rolling cart in white. It was a general utility cart, not a printer stand, with a narrow footprint for its capacity. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks fourth because the cart was not made for printers, but the extra tiers make it handy for paper and supplies. Compared with the Pipishell, the heavy-duty frame is the selling point.

Choose it if you want one cart for the printer and general storage. The caveat is that it has no printer-specific features.
products.idealFor: One cart for a printer plus other supplies.
products.skipIf: You want a purpose-built printer stand.

products.name: Pipishell 3 Tier Rolling Cart, Metal Utility Cart with Wheels and Handle
products.verdict: Roll the printer into a corner and out again when needed.
products.description:
A three-tier metal cart with a built-in handle, rolling wheels and a white finish. It started life as a general utility cart. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks fifth because the handle makes it easy to maneuver, but the listing does not claim heavy-duty construction like the Simple Houseware. Its strength is the store-away approach.

Buy it if you want the printer out of sight most days. The caveat is that, as a generic cart, it lacks printer-specific touches.
products.idealFor: Wheeling a printer out only when needed.

products.name: WALI Computer Monitor Stand with Underneath Storage
products.verdict: A tiny desk riser for rooms with no floor space.
products.description:
A desktop riser platform with an underneath storage compartment and a compact footprint, priced under $25. It was designed as a monitor or laptop riser.

It ranks sixth because a riser puts the printer on your desk, which costs workspace, and it was not made for printers. For rooms with no floor at all, that is the only trade that works.

Choose it when the printer must sit on the desk. The caveat is that it takes desk space you may want for a monitor.
products.idealFor: Tiny rooms where the printer sits on the desk.
products.skipIf: You have floor space under the desk.

products.name: Liitrton Mobile CPU Stand, Adjustable Computer Tower Stand
products.verdict: A low rolling platform repurposed from a PC tower stand.
products.description:
A mobile CPU stand with adjustable width, rolling casters and a low compact platform, priced under $25. It was designed for computer towers, not printers.

It ranks seventh because it offers only a platform, with no shelf, drawer or cable control. The adjustable width lets it cradle different printer sizes, and it is the smallest footprint here.

Pick it only if you want the lowest possible profile. The caveat is that it needs repurposing and holds just one printer.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the smallest footprint.
products.skipIf: You want a drawer or shelf.

products.name: Sywhitta 3-Tier Plastic Rolling Utility Cart with Handle
products.verdict: The lightest cart here, best for a light compact printer.
products.description:
A three-tier plastic rolling cart with a built-in handle and a white finish, and the lightest pick in this list. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks last because a plastic frame suits lighter machines than the metal carts. Its low weight makes it simple to move between rooms.

Choose it for a lightweight compact printer on a budget. The caveat is that plastic is less sturdy than metal, so heavier printers belong elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Light compact printers on a budget.

methodology.description: Stands built for printers ranked above repurposed carts and risers.

methodology.title: Footprint
methodology.description: Floor and desk space used, since small rooms cannot spare much.

methodology.title: Mobility
methodology.description: Casters, handles and locking wheels make a stand easy to move.

methodology.title: Storage and cables
methodology.description: Drawers, shelves and cable channels reduce clutter around the printer.

methodology.title: Build material
methodology.description: Metal frames scored above plastic for steadier support.

whatMatters.detail: Measure your printer's width and depth and compare it to the stand's top. A printer that overhangs is unsafe. Look for the tabletop dimensions in the title.
Paper trays and scanner lids need room to open. A stand too low under a shelf blocks them. Check the height against your space.
Casters make the stand mobile, and locking ones stop it rolling. Locks matter when you pull out a tray. Look for the word locking.
A rear channel keeps power and USB cords tidy. Without it, cables tangle on the floor. Look for a cable management mention.
Carts and risers were not built for printers and lack tailored features. They work, but check the fit yourself. The listing usually says if it is a utility cart.

faq.q: Can I use a utility cart for a printer?
faq.a: Yes, but check the tier size against your printer. The three carts here were not designed for printers.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with printer stands?
faq.a: Ignoring tray and lid clearance. The printer needs room to open.
Yes, since a rolling stand can shift when you pull a tray. The HUANUO lists locking casters.
A rear channel like the HUANUO's keeps cords tidy. Otherwise, use clips along the frame.

faq.q: Will a plastic cart hold a printer?
faq.a: It may suit a light compact printer. Heavier units belong on metal.

faq.q: Can a monitor riser hold a printer?
faq.a: The WALI is a monitor riser and not made for printers, so check your printer's size and weight first.

finalTake: For most small spaces, the HUANUO is the sensible printer stand with cable control and a drawer. The YAOHUOO fits bigger machines, and the HOOBRO suits dorms. Use a cart only when you want extra storage, and the WALI only when the printer must sit on the desk.
